pluss::subsp::stats::ts::TsPartition¶

Splits a series into consecutive training and test windows for honest forecast evaluation.

Signature¶

ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(std::int64_t num_observations, std::int64_t num_test_sets, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});
ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::sliding_window(std::int64_t num_observations, std::int64_t num_test_sets, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});
ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::holdout(std::int64_t num_observations, double holdout = 0.1, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});

Construction¶

Built by one of three factories; a partition holds only index ranges, not data.

State¶

A partition reports type(), direction(), num_observations(), num_test_sets(), gap_size(), max_lag() and step_size(), and its windows.

Methods¶

expanding_window¶

ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(std::int64_t num_observations, std::int64_t num_test_sets, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});

Windows whose training set starts at observation 0 and grows from one fold to the next: each test set is tested on a model trained on everything before it (up to max_train_size). Use it when old data stay relevant.

std::int64_t num_observations

Length of the series (greater than 1).

std::int64_t num_test_sets

Number of folds k (greater than 0).

const ts::PartitionOptions& options

Sizes, gap, buffer and direction; see PartitionOptions.

Returns. A TsPartition.

Errors. The requested sizes must fit k folds in n observations. max_lag must be smaller than the smallest training set.

sliding_window¶

ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::sliding_window(std::int64_t num_observations, std::int64_t num_test_sets, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});

Windows whose training set has fixed length train_size and slides forward with the test set. Use it when only recent data are relevant.

std::int64_t num_observations

Length of the series.

std::int64_t num_test_sets

Number of folds.

const ts::PartitionOptions& options

Sizes, gap, buffer and direction.

Returns. A TsPartition.

Errors. The requested sizes must fit in n observations.

holdout¶

ts::TsPartition ts::TsPartition::holdout(std::int64_t num_observations, double holdout = 0.1, const ts::PartitionOptions& options = {});

A single split: the last holdout fraction (if below 1) or count (if an integer ≥ 1) of the observations is the test set, preceded by gap_size unused observations and the training set.

std::int64_t num_observations

Length of the series.

double holdout

The test fraction in (0, 1), or a count of observations (an integer ≥ 1); default 0.1.

const ts::PartitionOptions& options

Gap, buffer and direction.

Returns. A TsPartition with one window.

Errors. holdout must be positive; a value of 1 or more must be an integer.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

The default windows: the last test set ends at the end of the series, and the three sizes are a quarter of the series each.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n, int offset) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + offset + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
// y_t = 0.5 y_{t-1} + 1.0 x_t + 0.3 x_{t-1} + 0.3 e_t with x_t = 0.8 x_{t-1} + 2 u_t: a response driven by its own past and by an exogenous series x.
struct Data {
  Series x, y;
};
Data make_data(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n, 0), u = noise(n, 7000);
  std::vector<double> x(n), y(n);
  double xp = 0.0, yp = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    const double xt = 0.8 * xp + 2.0 * u[t];
    const double yt = 0.5 * yp + 1.0 * xt + 0.3 * xp + 0.3 * e[t];
    x[t] = xt;
    y[t] = yt;
    xp = xt;
    yp = yt;
  }
  return {pluss::make_series(x, {n, 1}, f64), pluss::make_series(y, {n}, f64)};
}

int main() {
  std::cout << "expanding window\n";
  const auto expanding = ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(100, 3);
  for (const auto& w : expanding.windows())
    std::cout << "  train " << std::setw(3) << w.train_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.train_end + 1 << "   test " << std::setw(3) << w.test_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.test_end + 1 << "\n";
  std::cout << "sliding window\n";
  const auto sliding = ts::TsPartition::sliding_window(100, 3);
  for (const auto& w : sliding.windows())
    std::cout << "  train " << std::setw(3) << w.train_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.train_end + 1 << "   test " << std::setw(3) << w.test_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.test_end + 1 << "\n";
}

Output

expanding window
  train   1 -  25   test  26 -  50
  train   1 -  50   test  51 -  75
  train   1 -  75   test  76 - 100
sliding window
  train   1 -  25   test  26 -  50
  train  26 -  50   test  51 -  75
  train  51 -  75   test  76 - 100

Example 2¶

A gap leaves observations unused between training and test, and the sizes adapt so the windows still fit; giving only test_size makes the step equal to it.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n, int offset) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + offset + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
// y_t = 0.5 y_{t-1} + 1.0 x_t + 0.3 x_{t-1} + 0.3 e_t with x_t = 0.8 x_{t-1} + 2 u_t: a response driven by its own past and by an exogenous series x.
struct Data {
  Series x, y;
};
Data make_data(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n, 0), u = noise(n, 7000);
  std::vector<double> x(n), y(n);
  double xp = 0.0, yp = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    const double xt = 0.8 * xp + 2.0 * u[t];
    const double yt = 0.5 * yp + 1.0 * xt + 0.3 * xp + 0.3 * e[t];
    x[t] = xt;
    y[t] = yt;
    xp = xt;
    yp = yt;
  }
  return {pluss::make_series(x, {n, 1}, f64), pluss::make_series(y, {n}, f64)};
}

int main() {
  ts::PartitionOptions gap;
  gap.gap_size = 2;
  const auto gapped = ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(100, 3, gap);
  for (const auto& w : gapped.windows())
    std::cout << "gap 2:  train " << std::setw(3) << w.train_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.train_end + 1 << "   test " << std::setw(3) << w.test_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.test_end + 1 << "\n";
  ts::PartitionOptions test10;
  test10.test_size = 10;
  const auto tens = ts::TsPartition::sliding_window(100, 4, test10);
  for (const auto& w : tens.windows())
    std::cout << "test 10: train " << std::setw(3) << w.train_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.train_end + 1 << "   test " << std::setw(3) << w.test_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.test_end + 1 << "\n";
}

Output

gap 2:  train   1 -  26   test  29 -  52
gap 2:  train   1 -  50   test  53 -  76
gap 2:  train   1 -  74   test  77 - 100
test 10: train   1 -  60   test  61 -  70
test 10: train  11 -  70   test  71 -  80
test 10: train  21 -  80   test  81 -  90
test 10: train  31 -  90   test  91 - 100

Example 3¶

A forward expanding window starts from a given training length; a holdout is a single split; max_lag adds a buffer before the test set.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n, int offset) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + offset + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
// y_t = 0.5 y_{t-1} + 1.0 x_t + 0.3 x_{t-1} + 0.3 e_t with x_t = 0.8 x_{t-1} + 2 u_t: a response driven by its own past and by an exogenous series x.
struct Data {
  Series x, y;
};
Data make_data(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n, 0), u = noise(n, 7000);
  std::vector<double> x(n), y(n);
  double xp = 0.0, yp = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    const double xt = 0.8 * xp + 2.0 * u[t];
    const double yt = 0.5 * yp + 1.0 * xt + 0.3 * xp + 0.3 * e[t];
    x[t] = xt;
    y[t] = yt;
    xp = xt;
    yp = yt;
  }
  return {pluss::make_series(x, {n, 1}, f64), pluss::make_series(y, {n}, f64)};
}

int main() {
  ts::PartitionOptions forward;
  forward.direction = ts::Direction::Forward;
  forward.min_train_size = 40;
  forward.step_size = 20;
  const auto forwarded = ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(100, 3, forward);
  for (const auto& w : forwarded.windows())
    std::cout << "forward: train " << std::setw(3) << w.train_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.train_end + 1 << "   test " << std::setw(3) << w.test_start + 1 << " - " << std::setw(3) << w.test_end + 1 << "\n";
  const auto h = ts::TsPartition::holdout(100, 0.2).window(0);
  std::cout << "holdout: train " << h.train_start + 1 << " - " << h.train_end + 1 << "   test " << h.test_start + 1 << " - " << h.test_end + 1 << "\n";
  ts::PartitionOptions lag;
  lag.max_lag = 5;
  const auto w = ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(100, 3, lag).window(0);
  std::cout << "buffer of the first test set: " << w.test_buffer_start + 1 << " - " << w.test_buffer_end + 1 << "\n";
}

Output

forward: train   1 -  40   test  41 -  60
forward: train   1 -  60   test  61 -  80
forward: train   1 -  80   test  81 - 100
holdout: train 1 - 80   test 81 - 100
buffer of the first test set: 21 - 25

Example 4¶

The index and mask views of a fold.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n, int offset) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + offset + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
// y_t = 0.5 y_{t-1} + 1.0 x_t + 0.3 x_{t-1} + 0.3 e_t with x_t = 0.8 x_{t-1} + 2 u_t: a response driven by its own past and by an exogenous series x.
struct Data {
  Series x, y;
};
Data make_data(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n, 0), u = noise(n, 7000);
  std::vector<double> x(n), y(n);
  double xp = 0.0, yp = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    const double xt = 0.8 * xp + 2.0 * u[t];
    const double yt = 0.5 * yp + 1.0 * xt + 0.3 * xp + 0.3 * e[t];
    x[t] = xt;
    y[t] = yt;
    xp = xt;
    yp = yt;
  }
  return {pluss::make_series(x, {n, 1}, f64), pluss::make_series(y, {n}, f64)};
}

int main() {
  const auto partition = ts::TsPartition::expanding_window(20, 3);
  const Series test_idx = partition.test(0);
  std::cout << "test indices of fold 0: ";
  for (auto i : test_idx.host<std::int64_t>()) std::cout << i << " ";
  std::cout << "\ntraining mask sum of fold 0: " << partition.training_mask(0).to(pluss::ScalarType::Float64).sum().item<double>() << "\n";
}

Output

test indices of fold 0: 5 6 7 8 9 
training mask sum of fold 0: 5
